verdicts.trueWording: They are farmers, stonecutters, blacksmiths, traders, prospectors, and children
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200, browser UA). Quote byte-exact in the boxed text under 'Tips For Running Phandalin in Your Games', immediately followed on the page by 'Source: Dragon of Icespire Peak', confirming the reprint attribution. The list runs trades then ends on children, exactly as claimed.

verdicts.trueWording: Modest inn for eating, resting, and gossip
verdicts.note: Quote byte-exact in the 'Key NPCs and Locations' table, Stonehill Inn row; the table's three columns are Location / Proprietor / Short description and all nine rows do carry a named proprietor. The universal 'verbless' limb fails on one row.
verdicts.unsupportedLimb: that EVERY row's short description is verbless - the Lionshield Coster row reads 'Supplies armor and weapons', a finite verb phrase (8 of 9 rows are verbless)

verdicts.note: Byte-exact in the 'Key NPCs and Locations' table, Proprietor column of the Stonehill Inn row. Given name plus surname with species and gender parenthesised is the table's consistent form (e.g. the Barthen's Provisions and Alderleaf Farm rows follow it).

verdicts.trueWording: the town's layout, from the muddy streets lined with cart tracks
verdicts.note: Byte-exact, straight apostrophe included, in the 'Visual Description' bullet under the 'Arrival in Phandalin' heading. The sentence is addressed to the DM and does begin the layout at street surface and cart tracks before moving to the buildings.

verdicts.trueWording: a newspaper that covers events in Phandalin
verdicts.note: Byte-exact in the opening body paragraph. In-world newspaper, handout, and the Phandalin adventures (Shattered Obelisk, Lost Mine of Phandelver) are all on the page. Caveat, not a failed limb: the page says 'Downloadable Handout' and supplies the image inline rather than printing the word 'free', and credits D&D Beyond / Mike Bernier rather than naming Wizards of the Coast.

verdicts.trueWording: Ches 25, Phandalin - Ambushed wagons, dead travelers, and a town
verdicts.note: Byte-exact including the en dash, opening the story headlined 'Goblin Ambush Shocks Travelers on Triboar Trail'. Ches is a Forgotten Realms month, so the dateline is in-world date plus settlement; the list that follows carries no finite verb.

verdicts.trueWording: Linene Graywind, owner of Lionshield Coster in Phandalin
verdicts.note: Byte-exact in the attribution of the first quoted speaker in the 'Goblin Ambush' story. Given name, surname, office ('owner'), institution ('Lionshield Coster'), then settlement ('in Phandalin') appear in exactly the claimed order.

verdicts.trueWording: said Toblen, the innkeeper of the Stonehill Inn
verdicts.note: Byte-exact in the section headed "Redbrands' Reign of Terror". Given name alone, then trade, then the institution he keeps, with no surname used here (the sister article's table gives it as Stonehill).

verdicts.trueWording: What is Townmaster Wester going to do to keep us safe?
verdicts.note: Byte-exact inside speech the paper reports from an anonymous townsperson in the 'Goblin Ambush' story. Office title plus surname with no given name; the same form recurs in the paper's own narrative prose ('a lack of resistance from Townmaster Wester').

verdicts.trueWording: Townminster Weston hasn't been of any help
verdicts.note: Byte-exact, curly apostrophe included, in the editorial section "What's in This Issue of the Phandalin Post?", while the reproduced handout text above it twice reads 'Townmaster Wester'. Both spellings sit in the one article and the commentary refers back to those same articles, so it is the same officer: title and surname both differ.

verdicts.trueWording: Boroftkrah is a settlement of orcs, half-orcs, and a few people
verdicts.note: Byte-exact as the opening sentence under the 'Boroftkrah and the Gods' heading; the sentence continues 'of other races in the Greying Wildlands', supplying the region. Page is dated Mar 9, 2020 and tagged 'Encounter Of The Week', matching the cited column and year.

verdicts.trueWording: the toolbox's ones for dungeons and settlement creation
verdicts.note: Byte-exact in the random-tables paragraph; the preceding paragraph opens 'First up, the toolbox: This is the least focused chapter of the book', locating the tables in that chapter. Byline Harvey Randall, and the piece reviews the 2024 DMG. Locator nit: the section's actual heading is 'Tools & boxes', not 'The toolbox'.

verdicts.trueWording: more of a bullet-point list of suggestions than a guide
verdicts.note: Byte-exact, same paragraph as 1194; the sentence completes 'to cooking up good ideas of your own', which carries the claim's 'inventing one's own' limb. The referent 'these' is the dungeon and settlement-creation tables named in the prior clause.

Byte-exact as an h3 in the episode contents list, sitting under the h2 'Adventure Environments - Settlements'; page title is 'GMJ 235: DMG Chapter 5: Adventure Environments', dated December 16, 2018. The page names the book only as 'Dungeon Master's Guide', but its 2018 date and the listed chapter structure (Chapters 1-5 across earlier episodes) fix it as the 2014 fifth-edition guide.

Byte-exact as a sibling h3 to 'Random Settlements' under the same 'Adventure Environments - Settlements' h2 of the episode contents list, so it is named as another chapter 5 section. Edition inferred from the page's December 16, 2018 date as for 1196.
